lambo_derive.description: Derive concepts from the current interaction into session memory. A concept is one fact, stated atomically and short enough that a later restatement of the same fact matches it, such as a decision with its reason. Good: 'Lease TTL is 45s because it must exceed the 15s shutdown budget'. Bad: a paragraph narrating what you did and found. It is not a log: record activity with lambo_record_action. To group facts under a decision, send each as its own concept and add parent_of pairs with the decision as parent and each fact as child. When a concept rests on a ruling or decision already in memory, cite it by id (the 8 hex characters recall shows) in that concept's depends_on: it must already exist and match exactly one concept, or the whole call is refused. When a concept says an existing one is wrong, name that one the same way in the concept's against: it records the contradiction, newer against older, and changes no score. created_at is stamped server-side. event_time is optional RFC3339 historical about-time, such as a commit or document date; omit it for a live fact, which is about now. Returns as soon as the input is validated and ordered — the write is applied in the background and the ack carries a receipt id. The outcome is piggybacked on your next tool response; to wait for it, call lambo_stats with that receipt and a wait_ms. On a store with vector search each concept is embedded with the whole call's text, so a concept sent alone may be at most 8189 bytes; a longer call is refused before the ack, naming the part that is too long. scope (optional) writes to one of this session's shared layers instead; writes to different sessions have no ordering between them.

against.description:
Optional: up to 8 existing concepts this one contradicts, such as an
older belief a newer observation shows is wrong. Name each as for
`depends_on`: its id (the 8 hex characters recall shows) or full
node id (its exact content also works). Each must already exist in
the session the write goes to and match exactly one concept other
than this one, or the whole call is refused before the ack and
nothing is written. Recorded as this concept contradicting each; it is not evidence for
or against either and changes no score. At most 32 across the call.

content.description:
The concept text: one fact, stated atomically and short — a sentence,
not a paragraph or a log of what you did.

depends_on.description:
Optional: up to 8 existing concepts this one rests on, such as the
ruling a decision applies. Cite each by its id: the 8 hex characters
recall shows, or its full node id (its exact content also works).
Each must already exist in this session and match exactly one
concept; one that does not, or that names this concept itself,
refuses the whole call before the ack and writes nothing. Recorded as
this concept depending on each, which makes the cited concept
load-bearing. At most 32 across the call.

WireConceptType.description:
What kind of thing a concept is. Pick the one that fits the content best:

- `entity` — a named thing: a person, service, file, table, or component.
- `logic` — a rule, decision, or piece of reasoning about how things work.
- `constraint` — a requirement or limit that must keep holding.
- `resource` — something produced, consumed, or acted on by the work.
- `observation` — something noticed in passing; the weakest kind, and
  the only one that can later be demoted.

WireReference.description:
One `depends_on` or `against` entry: an existing concept, by the id
recall shows, its full node id or its exact content.

agent_id.description:
Id of the agent making this call. Use one stable id for the agent's
whole life, never one per call, task or topic (good: your model or
client id, such as `claude-opus-5-5` or `gpt-5.6`, with a stable
instance suffix such as `-worker-2` if several run at once; bad:
`b1-review`, `implement-m12`). Caller-asserted and unverified: work is
recorded under exactly the id you send, so a stable id keeps your
attribution whole. Agents sharing an id share soft locks and can
release each other's; concurrent agents that must keep out of each
other's edits need distinct stable ids.

concepts.description: Concepts to derive from this interaction.

event_time.description:
Optional RFC3339 historical about-time for this evidence, such as a
commit or document date. Omit it for a live fact, which is about now.
No additional date-range bounds are applied.

parent_of.description:
Optional `(parent, child)` hierarchy pairs. Both ends resolve (and may
be created) as concepts.

scope.description:
Optional: the session to write to. Omit it for this session; name
one of its layers (as `get_info` lists them), such as `general`, to
write there instead. Writes to different sessions have no ordering
between them, and every id or text a write cites must name a concept
in the session it writes to.

lambo_derive_image.description: Derive one image concept into session memory: a caption, plus either the image itself (image: mime and base64 data, embedded by this server) or a vector you computed in this session's embedding space (vector: values and contract, from lambo_stats embedding_contract). Send exactly one of image or vector. The concept's content is the caption plus [image:<image_id>] and its vector is the image's, so a text recall finds it; the same caption and image_id derived again is the same concept. created_at is stamped server-side; event_time, parent_of, scope, the ack and its receipt work as for lambo_derive.

WireEmbeddingContract.description: An embedding space: copy it from `lambo_stats`' `embedding_contract`.

model.description:
Model string, exactly as `lambo_stats` reports it (omit or null for
the server default).

data.description:
The image bytes in base64 (standard alphabet, padded), on one line,
with no `data:` prefix. At most 2 MiB decoded, and at most 4096 pixels
a side.

mime.description:
The image's media type, which must match its bytes: `image/png`,
`image/jpeg` or `image/webp`.

WireImageConceptType.description:
What kind of thing the image is. One of `entity`, `logic`, `constraint`,
`resource` (an image cannot be an `observation`).

WireVector.description: A vector you computed for the image, in this session's embedding space.

contract.description:
The embedding space the vector was computed in. It must equal this
session's `embedding_contract` exactly.

values.description:
The components, `dim` of them. Lambo normalizes the vector to unit
length.

agent_id.description:
Id of the agent making this call. Use one stable id for the agent's
whole life, never one per call, task or topic (good: your model or
client id, such as `claude-opus-5-5` or `gpt-5.6`, with a stable
instance suffix such as `-worker-2` if several run at once; bad:
`b1-review`, `implement-m12`). Caller-asserted and unverified: work is
recorded under exactly the id you send, so a stable id keeps your
attribution whole. Agents sharing an id share soft locks and can
release each other's; concurrent agents that must keep out of each
other's edits need distinct stable ids.

caption.description:
What the image is, in words. It is the concept's text: keyword recall
and the recall display read it. It may not contain an image suffix
of its own (`[image:<id>]`). With the suffix Lambo appends, the
content must fit in 16384 bytes: a caption of at most 16375 bytes less
the image id's length (16359 with the default 16-character id).

event_time.description:
Optional RFC3339 historical about-time for this evidence, such as a
commit or document date. Omit it for a live fact, which is about now.
No additional date-range bounds are applied.

image.description:
The image itself, for this server to embed. Send exactly one of
`image` and `vector`. The embedder may resize it (EmbeddingGemma 2:
to a 768 px longer side); send the same rendition of an image when
you need identical vectors.

image_id.description:
Your id for this image: 1 to 64 lowercase letters and digits. The
concept's content is the caption plus `[image:<image_id>]`; the same
caption and id derived again is the same concept. Omit it for an id
made from a digest of what you send: the image's bytes, or the
normalized vector.

parent_of.description:
Optional `(parent, child)` hierarchy pairs. Both ends resolve (and may
be created) as concepts; name the image concept by its content,
`caption [image:<image_id>]`.

scope.description:
Optional: the session to write to. Omit it for this session; name
one of its layers (as `get_info` lists them), such as `general`, to
write there instead. Writes to different sessions have no ordering
between them, and every id or text a write cites must name a concept
in the session it writes to.

vector.description:
A vector you computed for the image instead (accepted only when the
operator enabled client vectors). Send exactly one of `image` and
`vector`.

lambo_inspect.description: Inspect the neighbourhood around a concept: its type, canonization status, blast radius, the dependents it counts, why it is or is not promoted next, and typed edges out to a depth.

agent_id.description:
Id of the agent making this call. Use one stable id for the agent's
whole life, never one per call, task or topic (good: your model or
client id, such as `claude-opus-5-5` or `gpt-5.6`, with a stable
instance suffix such as `-worker-2` if several run at once; bad:
`b1-review`, `implement-m12`). Caller-asserted and unverified: work is
recorded under exactly the id you send, so a stable id keeps your
attribution whole. Agents sharing an id share soft locks and can
release each other's; concurrent agents that must keep out of each
other's edits need distinct stable ids.

depth.description: Hops out from the focus (default 2, max 5).

focus.description:
Concept content, a node UUID, or the short-form id rendered in recall
blocks, to centre the neighbourhood on.

scope.description:
Optional: the session to inspect in. Omit it for this session; name
one of its layers (as `get_info` lists them) to inspect a concept
there, such as a recall hit from that layer, whose id belongs to it.

lambo_recall.description: Recall relevant memory for a query and return the Lambo context block (canonical markers, blast-radius warnings, conflict lines).

WireEmbeddingContract.description: An embedding space: copy it from `lambo_stats`' `embedding_contract`.

model.description:
Model string, exactly as `lambo_stats` reports it (omit or null for
the server default).

data.description:
The image bytes in base64 (standard alphabet, padded), on one line,
with no `data:` prefix. At most 2 MiB decoded, and at most 4096 pixels
a side.

mime.description:
The image's media type, which must match its bytes: `image/png`,
`image/jpeg` or `image/webp`.

WireQueryVector.description: A query vector you computed, in this session's embedding space.

contract.description:
The embedding space the vector was computed in. It must equal this
session's `embedding_contract` exactly.

values.description:
The components, `dim` of them. Lambo normalizes the vector to unit
length.

agent_id.description:
Id of the agent making this call. Use one stable id for the agent's
whole life, never one per call, task or topic (good: your model or
client id, such as `claude-opus-5-5` or `gpt-5.6`, with a stable
instance suffix such as `-worker-2` if several run at once; bad:
`b1-review`, `implement-m12`). Caller-asserted and unverified: work is
recorded under exactly the id you send, so a stable id keeps your
attribution whole. Agents sharing an id share soft locks and can
release each other's; concurrent agents that must keep out of each
other's edits need distinct stable ids.

image.description:
Optional: recall what is close to this image, for this server to
embed (when its embedder embeds images). Send at most one of `image`
and `query_vector`. Not stored. The embedder may resize it
(EmbeddingGemma 2: to a 768 px longer side); send the same rendition
of an image when you need identical vectors.

max_tokens.description: Token budget for the rendered context block.

query.description:
Natural-language query. Required, unless you send `image` or
`query_vector`; beside either it is optional and its words still
match concept text.

query_vector.description:
Optional: recall what is close to a vector you computed, in this
session's embedding space (accepted only when the operator enabled
client vectors). Send at most one of `image` and `query_vector`. Not
stored.

scope.description:
Optional: read one session only. Omit it to read this session
together with its shared layers (when the operator configured any);
name this session, or one of its layers (as `get_info` lists them),
to read that session alone.

top_k.description: Hits to return. Defaults to the session config's `default_top_k`.

traversal_depth.description: Graph traversal depth for phase 2 expansion.

lambo_record_action.description: Record an action the agent took, with what it produces, modifies and depends on. This is where activity goes: name the act in a short line (e.g. 'merged PR #52'), not a narrative. A fact or decision that later work should recall is a concept for lambo_derive. When the action relied on a ruling or decision from memory, cite it by id (the 8 hex characters recall shows) in depends_on. When the action showed a concept in memory to be wrong, name it the same way in against. created_at is stamped server-side. event_time is optional RFC3339 historical about-time, such as a commit or document date; omit it for a live fact, which is about now. Returns as soon as the input is validated and ordered — the write is applied in the background and the ack carries a receipt id, resolved the same way as lambo_derive's. scope (optional) writes to one of this session's shared layers instead, where a relative file path is refused; writes to different sessions have no ordering between them.

WireReference.description:
One `depends_on` or `against` entry: an existing concept, by the id
recall shows, its full node id or its exact content.

WireResource.description:
One entry in a `lambo_record_action` resource list (`produces`,
`modifies`, `depends_on`). A plain string on the wire, with the same
per-string size cap the runtime enforces, so a client can pre-validate an
entry without a round trip.

action.description: The action taken — becomes a `Resource` concept.

against.description:
Optional: up to 8 existing concepts this action contradicts, such as a
belief the action showed to be wrong. Name each by its id (the 8 hex
characters recall shows) or full node id (its exact content also
works). Unlike `depends_on`, nothing is ever created: each must
already exist in the session the write goes to and match exactly one
concept, or the whole call is refused before the ack and nothing is
written.

agent_id.description:
Id of the agent making this call. Use one stable id for the agent's
whole life, never one per call, task or topic (good: your model or
client id, such as `claude-opus-5-5` or `gpt-5.6`, with a stable
instance suffix such as `-worker-2` if several run at once; bad:
`b1-review`, `implement-m12`). Caller-asserted and unverified: work is
recorded under exactly the id you send, so a stable id keeps your
attribution whole. Agents sharing an id share soft locks and can
release each other's; concurrent agents that must keep out of each
other's edits need distinct stable ids.

depends_on.description:
Things this action depends on (`Dependency` edges). To cite a ruling
or decision you relied on, give its id: the 8 hex characters recall
shows, or its full node id. An id names that existing concept; a
short id several concepts share is refused. Any other entry, and an
id that names no concept, names a concept by its text, created if
new.

event_time.description:
Optional RFC3339 historical about-time for this evidence, such as a
commit or document date. Omit it for a live fact, which is about now.
No additional date-range bounds are applied.

scope.description:
Optional: the session to write to. Omit it for this session; name
one of its layers (as `get_info` lists them), such as `general`, to
write there instead. Writes to different sessions have no ordering
between them, and every id or text a write cites must name a concept
in the session it writes to.

lambo_reserve.description: Take a soft lock on a memory node before editing it (or release one). Reservations are advisory and do not survive a server restart. The lock is held under the agent_id you send, which is caller-asserted and unverified: a distinct id gets a distinct lock, and callers sharing an id share the lock. scope (optional) names one of this session's shared layers, for a node from that layer.

agent_id.description:
Id of the agent making this call — the identity the lock is held under.
Use one stable id for the agent's whole life, never one per call, task
or topic (good: `claude-opus-5-5`, `gpt-5.6`, with a stable instance
suffix such as `-worker-2` if several run at once; bad: `b1-review`).
Caller-asserted and unverified: locks are cooperative. Distinct ids
contend: reserving a node another id holds is refused, naming the
holder. Two callers sending the SAME id share one lock and can release
each other's.

node_id.description:
Node to reserve, as a UUID string (from `lambo_recall` or
`lambo_inspect`).

release.description: Release this agent's existing soft lock instead of taking one.

scope.description:
Optional: the session the node belongs to. Omit it for this
session; name one of its layers (as `get_info` lists them) to reserve
or release a node there, such as a recall hit from that layer, whose
id belongs to it.

lambo_saints.description: List the session's canonical memories — concepts that earned Canonical status through the audited transition path. scope (optional) lists one of this session's shared layers instead.

agent_id.description:
Id of the agent making this call. Use one stable id for the agent's
whole life, never one per call, task or topic (good: your model or
client id, such as `claude-opus-5-5` or `gpt-5.6`, with a stable
instance suffix such as `-worker-2` if several run at once; bad:
`b1-review`, `implement-m12`). Caller-asserted and unverified: work is
recorded under exactly the id you send, so a stable id keeps your
attribution whole. Agents sharing an id share soft locks and can
release each other's; concurrent agents that must keep out of each
other's edits need distinct stable ids.

scope.description:
Optional: the session to list. Omit it for this session; name one of
its layers (as `get_info` lists them) to list that layer's canonical
memories.

lambo_stats.description: Session health: flush lag, write-behind log depth, background write queue depth, node/edge/concept counts, canonization progress and degraded state. Pass a receipt from a lambo_derive or lambo_record_action ack to ask what happened to that one write, and wait_ms to wait for it to be applied first.

agent_id.description:
Id of the agent making this call. Use one stable id for the agent's
whole life, never one per call, task or topic (good: your model or
client id, such as `claude-opus-5-5` or `gpt-5.6`, with a stable
instance suffix such as `-worker-2` if several run at once; bad:
`b1-review`, `implement-m12`). Caller-asserted and unverified: work is
recorded under exactly the id you send, so a stable id keeps your
attribution whole. Agents sharing an id share soft locks and can
release each other's; concurrent agents that must keep out of each
other's edits need distinct stable ids.

receipt.description:
A write receipt id from a `lambo_derive` or `lambo_record_action` ack.
Answers what happened to that one write: applied, failed, dropped,
pending, expired, restart-lost or never-issued. Receipts are scoped to
the agent that created them.

wait_ms.description:
With `receipt`, wait up to this many milliseconds for the write to be
applied before answering — the opt-in synchrony that restores
read-your-writes when you need it. Clamped to the server's own maximum.
Ignored without `receipt`.

The published maximum is [`crate::writeq::RECEIPT_WAIT_MAX`] in
milliseconds — a client that sends more is clamped to it rather than
refused, and `the_published_wait_maximum_is_the_real_one` pins the
literal below to the constant (T88-H4 requires a *published* maximum,
and `schemars` takes a literal).
